== PlayStation 2 NVM OSD configuration block checksum ==
''Suggested page: PS2 → EEPROM / NVRAM (NVM) Format → Config Block Checksum.''

The PlayStation 2 MechaCon chip contains 1,024 bytes (1 KiB) of non-volatile EEPROM (NVM). System configuration (language, video mode, aspect ratio, timezone, daylight saving, and parental controls) is organized into 16-byte blocks accessed through MechaCon S-commands <code>0x40..0x43</code> (exposed to the Emotion Engine via <code>XCDVDMAN</code> / <code>XCDVDFSV</code> RPC functions <code>0x0E..0x11</code>).

=== Block format and layouts ===
Each 16-byte configuration block comprises '''15 bytes of data''' followed by '''1 byte of checksum''':
* <code>block[0..14]</code>: 15 payload bytes.
* <code>block[15]</code>: 8-bit checksum.

The primary system configuration (Area 1, Block 1) is located according to console ROM generation:
* '''Layout 0''' (ROM < 1.70: 1.00 J, 1.50 devkit, 1.60): file offset '''<code>0x310..0x31F</code>'''.
* '''Layout 1''' (ROM ≥ 1.70: 2.00 E): file offset '''<code>0x2C0..0x2CF</code>'''.

=== The checksum algorithm ===
In Sony's IOP firmware (<code>XCDVDMAN</code> <code>FUN_00008348</code> in 2.00; <code>FUN_000072F0</code> in 1.60), the checksum is verified on read and generated on write as the '''lower 8 bits of the sum of the 15 data bytes''':

<syntaxhighlight lang="c">
u8 checksum = 0;
for (int i = 0; i < 15; i++) {
    checksum += block[i];
}
</syntaxhighlight>

* When reading a block (S-command <code>0x41</code>), if <code>block[15] != checksum</code>, the MechaCon driver flags error '''status 1'''.
* When writing a block (S-command <code>0x42</code>), the IOP automatically computes <code>checksum</code> and writes it to byte 15. The EE RPC returns only the 15 verified data bytes to OSDSYS.

=== The PCSX2 default NVM checksum bug ===
When PCSX2 generates a new default <code>.NVM</code> file (via <code>cdvdCreateNewNVM</code>), it initializes Area 1 Block 1 with pre-populated regional defaults:
* English: <code>30 21 00 00 00 70 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 [41]</code>
* Japanese: <code>20 20 00 00 00 70 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 [30]</code>
* Chinese: <code>30 2B 00 00 00 70 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 [4B]</code>

'''The defect''': PCSX2 stores the checksum with '''bit 7 stripped''' (<code>sum & 0x7F</code>):
* English data sum is <code>0xC1</code> (193). Stored checksum is '''<code>0x41</code>'''.
* Japanese data sum is <code>0xB0</code> (176). Stored checksum is '''<code>0x30</code>'''.
* Chinese data sum is <code>0xCB</code> (203). Stored checksum is '''<code>0x4B</code>'''.

=== Runtime consequence on real BIOSes ===
When an authentic BIOS (1.50, 1.60, or 2.00) boots against this PCSX2 default file:
# <code>XCDVDMAN</code> computes the full 8-bit sum (<code>0xC1</code>), compares it against the stored byte (<code>0x41</code>), and detects a mismatch, reporting status 1.
# OSDSYS re-attempts <code>ReadConfig</code> while <code>status & 0x81</code> is non-zero (routine <code>0x203DD0..0x203E04</code>).
# On retry, PCSX2's internal block cursor is past the end, causing it to return a zero-filled buffer.
# Because the checksum of 15 zero bytes is trivially 0, the zeroed block passes validation.
# OSDSYS consumes the all-zero block: config is flagged as "uninitialized" (packed byte <code>0x11</code> bit 7 is clear).
# Consequently, '''OSDSYS launches the first-boot setup wizard''' on first boot.
# When the user completes the setup wizard, OSDSYS writes back a properly checksummed block (e.g. ending in <code>0xE0</code> or <code>0xBF</code>), correcting the file on disk.

Thus, the initial configuration values PCSX2 intends to provision are never actually honored by retail BIOS code.

''Source: [https://github.com/NamasteJasutin/PSXBootInspectionTool PSXBootInspectionTool], notes/research/rom1_erom_nvm.md §3.1, §3.4.''
